sections.title: Multiple Representations of Relationships
sections.learning_target: Students will connect tables, graphs, equations, and contexts that represent the same relationship.
i_cans: I can construct a table, graph, equation, or context from another representation of the same relationship.
I can use features in one representation to work with a related table, graph, equation, or context.
I can determine whether two representations belong to the same relationship using evidence from values, rates, or patterns.

spiral.intro: Connect tables, graphs, equations, and contexts that represent the same relationship.
spiral.review: Interpret and create graphs on the coordinate plane while connecting points, axes, intercepts, and graphical information to mathematical situations.
spiral.mastery: Solve inequalities, represent solution sets graphically, and interpret solutions in context.

sections.title: Inputs, Outputs, and Functions
sections.learning_target: Students will interpret functions as rules that connect inputs and outputs without relying on formal domain and range language.
i_cans: I can formulate a rule that connects inputs to outputs in a table, graph, equation, or context.
I can apply an input-output rule to generate missing values and ordered pairs.
I can assess whether a rule gives one output for each input in a situation.

spiral.intro: Interpret functions as rules that connect inputs and outputs without relying on formal domain and range language.
spiral.review: Identify patterns and represent relationships using input-output rules, tables, words, and symbols.
spiral.mastery: Evaluate numerical and algebraic expressions correctly using substitution and order of operations.

sections.title: Function Families
sections.learning_target: Students will recognize common function families from graphs, tables, equations, and contexts.
i_cans: I can design examples of linear, quadratic, exponential, and absolute value relationships using more than one representation.
I can extend patterns in tables, graphs, equations, and contexts to work with common function families.
I can critique a proposed function family choice using evidence from rate of change, shape, or equation structure.

spiral.intro: Recognize common function families from graphs, tables, equations, and contexts.
spiral.review: Recognize constant rate of change in tables, graphs, visual patterns, and situations.
spiral.mastery: Accurately perform operations with integers, fractions, and decimals while interpreting results in mathematical and contextual situations.

sections.title: Expressions and Structure
sections.learning_target: Students will interpret and rewrite algebraic expressions by identifying structure, meaning, and equivalent forms.
i_cans: I can build equivalent expressions by using structure, grouping, and properties of operations.
I can apply rewriting strategies to make the meaning of an expression easier to work with.
I can determine whether two expressions are equivalent by using structure, substitution, or properties.

spiral.intro: Interpret and rewrite algebraic expressions by identifying structure, meaning, and equivalent forms.
spiral.review: Compare relationships using equations, graphs, tables, visual patterns, and contexts, then justify conclusions.
spiral.mastery: Analyze and rewrite algebraic expressions using properties of operations and algebraic structure.

sections.title: Equations as Models
sections.learning_target: Students will write, solve, and interpret equations that model situations.
i_cans: I can construct an equation that models a situation using meaningful quantities and operations.
I can use solution steps to solve an equation and connect the result to the situation.
I can predict whether a solution is reasonable by interpreting it in the original context.

spiral.intro: Write, solve, and interpret equations that model situations.
spiral.review: Represent linear relationships using tables, graphs, equations, and contextual descriptions.
spiral.mastery: Solve one-variable equations and interpret solutions within mathematical and contextual situations.

1.1.Graph: PLANNED — central to multiple-representation equivalence; WTC, Notes, and every Practice form use a graph.
1.1.Table: PLANNED — WTC, Notes, and every Practice form use input-output tables.
1.1.Context: PLANNED — distance/cost/time and other named quantities connect representations.

1.2.Graph: N/A for the Intro target — input/output rules, tables, mappings, and contexts carry the intended meaning; graph work remains available in other sections.
1.2.Equation: PLANNED — function rules are written and applied.
1.2.Table: PLANNED — primary input-output representation across Notes/Practice.
1.2.Context: PLANNED — students identify meaningful inputs and outputs in situations.

1.3.Graph: PLANNED — function-family shape is central; WTC, Notes, and every Practice form use a graph.
1.3.Equation: PLANNED — structure is used as family evidence.
1.3.Table: PLANNED — differences/ratios/patterns are used in every Practice form.
1.3.Context: PLANNED — family choice is interpreted in natural situations.

1.4.Graph: N/A for the Intro target — expression structure/equivalence is better represented with symbols, tables, context, area/tiles.
1.4.Equation: PLANNED — algebraic expressions/equivalent forms are the main symbolic representation.
1.4.Table: PLANNED — substitution/value tables are used to test equivalence.
1.4.Context: PLANNED — perimeter/cost/repeated-quantity expressions give terms meaning.

1.5.Graph: PLANNED for Review retrieval, not forced into Intro Practice — review work connects linear graphs; equation modeling remains the Intro focus.
1.5.Equation: PLANNED — primary model and solution representation.
1.5.Table: PLANNED — quantity tables organize contexts and support equation writing.
1.5.Context: PLANNED — every major family includes model/solution interpretation.
